newsitem.title: UK: Outright Brent falls as Iraq oil exports loom.
newsitem.headline: Outright Brent falls as Iraq oil exports loom.

text.p: North Sea crude oil markets saw action concentrate on the forward markets early on Wednesday as outright levels fell.
Traders said the price weakness was a combination of concern over the proximity of Iraqi barrels and a softer Brent crude oil market.
Outright September Brent on the IPE lost 22 cents to $19.30 a barrel by 1150 GMT.
Iraq's oil minister Amir Rasheed said on Wednesday that his country expects to resume oil exports under its oil-for-food deal with the U.N. in mid-August.

Late on Tuesday Iraq gave the U.N. its proposed August pricing formula putting Kirkuk to Europe at Dated Brent -$1.90 a barrel. This was some 10 cents firmer than traders had expected but most felt it was competitive.
"In the current market this is very competitive but it all depends on how much they end up selling," one lifter from the first crude sales deal said.
Many companies who bought Iraqi crude under the first oil-for-food sales tranche were in meetings over the morning discussing the volume they would buy for the period up to September 5.

"There's no point in comparing daily rates from before to what people will take now. It will depend on the size of the ship but we are interested in taking more than last time," a trader with a major said.

Trader pointed out that they had not as yet had any indications of Iraq's sales strategy and how Baghdad would differentiate the first short period to Sept 5 and sales in the following full 90 day period.
Shipbrokers said they saw heightened interest in ULCC, VLCC and one million barrel vessels loading out of Ceyhan in the August 16-25 period.
Intermonth spreads lost ground in a narrowing contango. Brent Sept/Oct and Oct/Nov moved to -10/-7 cents with the Sept/Oct trading at -9 cents.
CFD's for the next four weeks lost some 10-12 cents. The Aug 25-29 moved once at October -27 cents and twice at Oct -30 cents. The Aug 18-22 dropped 10 cents to trade at Oct -30 cents.
The only physical deal reported was an Ekofisk loading August 25 which sold to a refiner at dated Brent +27 cents - down from deals on Tuesday at dated +29 and +30 cents.
There was one Brent cargo in the paper chains.
Many traders expected Dated Brent to trade a few cents below September after two cargoes moved on Tuesday at September +3 and September +18 cents.
"There's someone there who wants the price down so we will see a low deal, probably today. The buying is very thin anyway," one refiner said.
